Then codified the whole flow as the /issue-fix project skill.

BUILT: parse_date accepts ISO 8601 timestamps, normalized to naive-UTC SECOND precision. The second-truncation is the load-bearing choice and it was NOT the first design — v1 rendered microseconds and justified it with an ASCII-ordering argument over the four started_at spellings I sampled from the live DB. codex review (gpt-5.6-sol medium) found the fifth spelling: epoch_ms_to_iso emits ...T14:00:00+00:00 on whole seconds, '+' (0x2B) sorts below '.' (0x2E), so a row at exactly the cursor instant was EXCLUDED — the silent-skip direction the normalization existed to prevent. Truncating to seconds makes the bound a lexical PREFIX of every spelling, which removes the fragile reasoning instead of patching its conclusion. /simplify separately caught that db send/push/pull passed parse_date as a bare argparse type=, which swallows the message, so the widened hint never reached users on the three subcommands the fix was about (-> shared date_arg + DATE_VOCABULARY).

CALIBRATION (the transferable one): an enumeration derived by SAMPLING the live database is not an enumeration. It gives the shapes that database happens to hold, not the shapes the code can emit. Grep the producers. My four-shape survey was empirically honest and still wrong, and every downstream argument inherited the gap. Second calibration: local green is not CI green — pushed #21's merge with a red run and did not look, compounded by './dev check | grep failed && git push' pushing ON failure since grep exits 0 on a match.

DECIDED: no develop branch (user proposed one; CLAUDE.md already rules it out with rationale and a not-before-1.0 revisit trigger, and the changelog half of the proposal is already the process). The real gap was that deferred items live in PR bodies, which are write-only after merge -> issues + roadmap node instead. Decompose deferrals by CAUSE not symptom: five findings collapsed into one absence (#32).

FILED: #31 aider local wall time in a UTC column; #32 timestamp coherence (thread opened); #33 12-char ULID prefixes collide 1-in-1005 (measured) and get_event silently returns the wrong event — its in-code deferral has a false premise ('random ULID portion' — chars 1-10 are timestamp) and a trigger measuring the wrong axis (table size, not events-per-millisecond), so it would never have fired.

NEXT ENTRY POINT: user runs /issue-fix on #31 next session — first real outing of the skill."}
